# APOD Ask

> A hands-on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) demo over NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD). Ask an astronomy question in natural language and get an answer grounded only in real APOD explanation texts, with the source images and videos shown.

APOD Ask is a learning and portfolio project by Melanie Stief. The whole RAG pipeline is deliberately visible: the question and every APOD explanation are embedded with Google's multilingual Gemini embedding model, the closest texts are retrieved by cosine similarity from a hosted Upstash Vector store, and Google Gemini writes the answer under a strict "answer only from these texts" grounding prompt. Questions can be asked in any language (e.g. German questions match the English APOD texts). The query and ingest paths both follow a clean-architecture split (domain, use cases with ports, infrastructure adapters), so the core never depends on Gemini, Upstash or NASA directly.

## Pages

- [Ask](https://nuxt-rag.netlify.app/): The main page: ask an astronomy question and get a grounded answer with the source images and videos.
- [How it works](https://nuxt-rag.netlify.app/how-it-works): The RAG pipeline as a four-step timeline (embed, retrieve, rank, generate) with real code excerpts.
- [About](https://nuxt-rag.netlify.app/about): The learning motivation and the exact tech stack.

## Stack

- Framework: Nuxt 4 + Vue, Nitro server routes
- Embeddings: Google Gemini `gemini-embedding-001` (multilingual, 768-dim, L2-normalized)
- Vector store: Upstash Vector (hosted, cosine similarity)
- Language model: Google Gemini (`gemini-flash-latest`) with a grounded prompt, returning a Zod-validated JSON reply (a decision, the answer, and the cited source ids)
- Data: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) API
- Hosting: Netlify
